articles.title: India were cheated: Durga Rao slams Pakistan over Blind Asia Cup final row - India Today
articles.summary: India were cheated: Durga Rao slams Pakistan over Blind Asia Cup final row India Today
articles.content: India's blind cricket team captain Durga Rao has expressed his disappointment over Pakistan being declared winners of the Men's Asia Cup for the Blind despite the final in Dhaka being abandoned without a ball being bowled. Calling the decision an injustice, Rao questioned the use of net run rate to determine the winner and said the Indian contingent was left shocked by the announcement.In an exclusive interview with India Today, Rao said the Indian team had been at the ground since 10 am on Friday, waiting for the rain to ease and the final to get underway. However, after hours of uncertainty, the Indian contingent was informed that Pakistan would be awarded the title on the basis of a superior run rate."We felt that we are in the ground from morning 10 onwards. The rain was continuously falling down. The umpires kept informing us that the match was delayed. They told us that the cut-off would be till 4.15 pm," Rao said."At 4 o'clock, they had called me, my manager and people from their team. They told us that due to the run rate, we are declaring Pakistan as winners."The decision left the Indian players and officials stunned, with Rao insisting that the tournament regulations did not provide for a team to be declared the winner on the basis of run rate when no play had taken place."If the rule had been there, we could have accepted it. But in the laws and whatever WBC rules were there, they had never mentioned that due to the run rate, the winners would be announced," he said."From my point of view, we never expected this because the rules were not there. We personally felt it was an injustice for us."NO CLEAR ANSWERSThe controversy intensified after the Indian contingent challenged the decision during discussions with the match officials. According to Rao, the team's manager raised several questions, particularly because not a single delivery had been bowled in the final.He said the Indian team wanted clarity on how the organisers had arrived at their decision but did not receive satisfactory explanations."When the match referee called us, my manager was asking questions because it was purely mentioned that if the match had happened, then you could have taken that call on net run rate," Rao said."But not even one ball had been bowled. Those were the questions our manager asked. At the same time, there was no proper answer from them."Rao also questioned the communication surrounding the decision, stressing that a tournament of the Asia Cup's stature required greater transparency from its organisers."This is not a small tournament. It is the Asia Cup, where all the big countries are playing. They have to clearly look at the rules and announce the decision. Our manager raised so many questions, but there were no proper answers," he added.INDIA'S PAKISTAN STANCEThe fallout has extended beyond the abandoned final, with the Cricket Association for the Blind in India (CABI) taking a strong position against future cricketing engagements with Pakistan.CABI has said India will not play Pakistan in the future following the controversy. Asked whether the players shared that position, Rao said the team would abide by the association's decision."Whatever the board says, CABI will take care of it. Whatever they say, we have to follow it and we will follow that. The association is the one that has that authority," he said.The controversy erupted after Pakistan were awarded the title despite the final being washed out in Dhaka. The Indian contingent objected to the use of net run rate to determine the winner, arguing that the teams should have been declared joint champions.According to the wider controversy surrounding the decision, the World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC) president and Pakistan Blind Cricket Council chief Sultan Shah reportedly overruled the technical committee's decision to declare India and Pakistan joint winners, following which Pakistan were announced as champions.India, who entered the tournament as defending champions, subsequently stayed away from the trophy presentation in protest.WANT JUSTICEFor Rao, the disappointment was not simply about missing out on a trophy. The Indian captain felt the decision should have been made by following the tournament's regulations and ensuring that both teams were given a fair hearing.While he left questions about the legality of the decision and the next course of action to the team's management, he reiterated that the Indian players felt badly let down by the outcome."Whatever decision has been taken by Pakistan, we feel it has been really unjust. Personally, we felt bad because the decision could have been better," Rao said."When there has been a loss, you have to follow that. When there are rules in WBC, you have to follow them and make sure there is proper communication as well."For the Indian blind cricket team, the controversy has left a bitter feeling after a final that never got underway. And with CABI now taking a firm position on future matches against Pakistan, the fallout from the Dhaka final could have consequences well beyond the tournament itself.- EndsMust Watch

articles.title: Maharashtra government forms CM-led panel to suggest names of metro stations in Mumbai, Pune and Nagpur - Deccan Herald
articles.summary: Maharashtra government forms CM-led panel to suggest names of metro stations in Mumbai, Pune and Nagpur Deccan Herald
articles.content: Mumbai: The Maharashtra government has constituted a six-member committee headed by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis to recommend to the Centre the naming and potential rechristening of metro railway stations in Mumbai, Pune and Nagpur metropolitan regions. . The panel has been asked to consider the cultural, historical and geographical significance of an area, local public sentiments and the need to avoid controversy while recommending names, according to a Government Resolution (GR) issued by the Urban Development Department (UDD) on November 18. . Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde , who holds the UDD portfolio, will be the co-chairperson of the panel. .A track change for Bengaluru's metro viability. The other members will include the Lok Sabha MP and MLA from the area concerned and the mayor or chairperson of the respective local self-government body, while the administrative head of the metro project implementing agency will act as Member-Secretary of the committee. . The committee will function under Rule 3(1) of the Centre's Metro Rail (Naming or Renaming of Stations) Rules, 2026, notified by the Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs in March this year. . As per the rules, the panel must consider six criteria, including cultural heritage, historical and geographical significance, sentiments of local residents, ease of pronunciation and consistency with the locality's identity, while suggesting names or renames of metro stations. .Maharashtra woman gets 4.5 acres back after 30-year land dispute over Rs 25,000 loan. It will also have to avoid confusion arising from identical or similar-sounding station names and balance the symbolic representation of leaders or deities without triggering a controversy, according to the GR. . Under the standard operating procedure, metro railway managements or implementing agencies will first scrutinise representations received for naming or renaming stations and submit detailed proposals to the state government. . The state UDD will place these proposals before the committee, whose recommendations will subsequently be forwarded to the Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs for approval.

articles.title: J&K wins India Sports Award for ‘Excellence in Promoting Sports’ - Rising Kashmir
articles.summary: J&K wins India Sports Award for ‘Excellence in Promoting Sports’ Rising Kashmir
articles.content: New Delhi, Nov 20: In a moment of immense pride and recognition, the Government of Jammu and Kashmir has been selected for the prestigious India Sports Award 2026 under the category “Best State/UT Promoting Sports” by the FICCI India Sports Awards Jury. The recognition acknowledges the Government's sustained efforts towards strengthening the sports ecosystem, promoting sporting culture and creating opportunities for young talent across Jammu & Kashmir. The award is a testament to the Government's commitment to nurture sporting excellence through development of sports infrastructure, strengthening grassroots sports initiatives, encouraging youth participation and providing a platform for aspiring athletes to showcase their talent at national and international levels. Over the years, Jammu & Kashmir has witnessed a renewed momentum in the sports sector, with focused interventions aimed at making sports an integral part of youth development, discipline, confidence-building and nation-building. The recognition assumes particular significance as it places Jammu and Kashmir among the leading states/UTs in the country in terms of promoting sports and institutionalising a vibrant sporting culture. The India Sports Awards 2026 ceremony was held today, at FICCI Federation House, New Delhi, as part of FICCI TURF 2026, the 16th Global Sports Summit. The award stands as an encouragement to the sporting fraternity, young athletes, coaches, sports administrators and all stakeholders who have contributed to the growth of sports in the Union Territory of J&K. This prestigious honour is not merely an award but a recognition of Jammu and Kashmir's growing sporting aspirations and its commitment to building a healthier, stronger and more empowered generation through sports. Naila Zahoor, Director Finance, Youth Services & Sports Department J&K, received the prestigious award on behalf of the Government of Jammu and Kashmir.

articles.title: French minister slams IOC's mandatory gene tests, calls them extreme violence - India Today
articles.summary: French minister slams IOC's mandatory gene tests, calls them extreme violence India Today
articles.content: France Sports Minister Marina Ferrari has strongly opposed the International Olympic Committee's (IOC) mandatory gene-testing policy for female athletes, describing the move as "extreme violence toward women" and a step backwards for women's rights.Ferrari said the tests raise serious ethical concerns and amount to discrimination against women, adding that she hoped the IOC would reconsider its eligibility rules ahead of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.The IOC introduced its new eligibility policy in March, ruling that participation in female-category events at the Olympic Games and other IOC competitions would be restricted to biological females. The policy requires athletes to undergo a mandatory gene test once in their careers to establish eligibility.The rules will come into effect at the Los Angeles Games in July 2028."I can't say for now if the IOC will backtrack on this, I hope so," Ferrari told reporters during a phone call on Friday. "Several international federations have already started putting them into place."WTA DECISION DRAWS FLAKFerrari also criticised the Women's Tennis Association (WTA) for introducing mandatory one-time gene testing for players seeking to compete at the 2028 Olympics.The WTA announced the change in July, updating its eligibility policy to include gender screening based on biological sex. The governing body said the move was aimed at preserving the integrity of women's professional tennis and maintaining fair competition.Ferrari described the decision as "depressing" and said around 60 per cent of French female athletes were opposed to gene testing."We consider it to be a form of extreme violence toward women, a clear discrimination," she said. "For me it's a clear regression in terms of women's rights, and I ask myself what will happen in 2030 when we will host the Winter Olympics."France is scheduled to host the 2030 Winter Olympics.FEARS TESTING COULD SPREADFerrari raised the issue during a two-day European Union meeting in Brussels focused on youth and sport. She said she had also been holding discussions with counterparts from other countries to build opposition to the policy."I am continuing to have bilateral talks with my counterparts. I think an awareness is happening and some countries are realising this concerns all female athletes," she said.The French minister also expressed concern that mandatory gender screening could extend beyond elite athletes competing at the Olympics and eventually affect younger participants in sport.Gender screening is already being implemented by several international sports governing bodies, including those overseeing athletics, skiing and boxing. The practice has faced criticism from human rights experts and activist groups over concerns about discrimination, privacy and the treatment of female athletes.The IOC has defended its new eligibility framework, saying it is designed to protect fairness, safety and integrity in women's sporting categories. Under the policy, transgender women are excluded from competing in the female category at the Olympics.- Ends

articles.title: State Sanctions Funds To Upgrade Baramati Airport - Deccan Chronicle
articles.summary: State Sanctions Funds To Upgrade Baramati Airport Deccan Chronicle
articles.content: Mumbai: Ten months after Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar died in a crash at Baramati airstrip, the Maharashtra government has sanctioned Rs 64.53 crore to upgrade the airport for night and all-weather landings, along with an annual recurring allocation of Rs 68.88 lakh for operations and staffing.The State General Administration Department issued a government resolution in this regard on Thursday. The funding will facilitate night-time and poor-visibility operations by non-scheduled operators (NSOPs) under Instrument Flight Rules (IFR). The decision follows the transfer of the airfield from the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation (MIDC) to the Maharashtra Airport Development Company (MADC) and approval by a state-level committee. Major components of the funding include Rs 12 crore for a 10,000-litre fire crash foam tender, Rs 10.56 crore for runway strip grading and drainage, Rs 6 crore for navigation and lighting aids, Rs 10.46 crore for perimeter security and a compound wall, Rs 5 crore for a prefabricated Air Traffic Control (ATC) tower-cum-fire station, Rs 6.88 crore for runway recarpeting and Runway End Safety Area (RESA) works, and Rs 9.52 crore towards GST, consultancy and insurance charges. The annual recurring allocation of Rs 68.88 lakh will cover utility expenses and the engagement of 21 contractual personnel, including management, security, firefighting and maintenance staff. Baramati MP Supriya Sule, a cousin of Ajit Pawar and a leader of the NCP (SP), welcomed the state government's sanction of Rs 64.53 crore for upgrading Baramati Airport, describing the move as “better late than never”. Sule also expressed regret over the timing of the release of funds. Referring to the fatal aircraft crash at the airstrip in January this year, which killed Ajit Pawar and four others, she remarked that if the funds had been approved earlier, the tragedy might have been averted and “Dada” (Ajit Pawar) might still have been alive. Ajit Pawar, the then Deputy Chief Minister, died in an aircraft crash at Baramati in Pune district on January 28 this year. A Learjet 45 aircraft operated by VSR Ventures Pvt Ltd crashed at Baramati airport on the morning of January 28 while en route from Mumbai to Baramati, killing Ajit Pawar and four others. The Maharashtra Criminal Investigation Department (CID) and the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), under the Ministry of Civil Aviation, are conducting separate inquiries into the incident.

Three players, Kochhar, Bhullar and Aryan Roopa Anand of RVR Delhi Blue Bulls GC were locked at 10-under after 54 holes of action over the last three. Then it took another two holes before Kochhar won on the second extra hole, as Bhullar, who had earlier regaled the crowd with monster putts over the past few weeks, missed a three-footer and Aryan too missed. articles.content: Mandaviya Urges Global Partners to Help India Become Sports Economy Union Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports Mansukh Mandaviya on Friday urged industry leaders, investors and international sporting institutions to partner with India in strengthening its sports ecosystem, calling for collective efforts to “Make in India, Play in India, and Grow with India” as the country aims to emerge as a global sports economy. Mansukh Mandaviya inaugurated the 16th edition of TURF, the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry’s (FICCI) Global Summit on Business of Sports, in New Delhi on Friday, as per a press release by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. Addressing the gathering, Mandaviya said, “Sports have emerged as a powerful instrument for youth development, social inclusion, economic opportunity and international cooperation.” He said, “Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India has placed sports at the centre of its nation-building agenda. Our approach is guided by a clear vision – creating opportunities for every aspiring athlete, from the playground to the podium.” The summit is being held under the theme “Powering India’s Sports Economy: Partnerships, Innovation & Global Leadership”. Highlighting the transformation of India's sporting ecosystem over the last 12 years, Mandaviya said, “Through initiatives such as Khelo India Mission, Fit India Movement, and Target Olympic Podium Scheme, we are expanding grassroots participation, identifying sporting talent and creating pathways towards high-performance sports.” The Union Cabinet recently approved the new Khelo India Scheme, with an outlay of Rs 36,441 crore for the next five years, to strengthen sports infrastructure, nurture talent, and promote sports development across the country. Speaking on the role of industry, Mandaviya said, “We recognise that the future of sports will be shaped, not only by athletes and sporting institutions, but also by a strong, competitive and innovation-driven sports industry.” The Government has approved the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme, with an outlay of Rs 1,856.67 crore, to make India a global hub for sports goods manufacturing and innovation. Mandaviya outlined India’s intent to host major international sporting events, aiming to host the Commonwealth Games 2030 in Ahmedabad, while also harbouring hopes of hosting the 2036 Olympics.
